entries.en:
This book presents itself as nothing more than a collection of absurd theories on the existence of ghosts, however there are parts written in a different tone.

"There is an innate power in the ghost realm, unlike the physical world it is not governed by the constraints of matter or the laws of physics. A ghost can conjure anything, any object or power they can simply call into being, much as we do when we dream. This however requires keen awareness of their condition, an understanding of their realm and their place within it. Most ghosts wander in a state of confusion, at the mercy of twisted thoughts and perceptions, but not all. There are those that have awakened, or perhaps never slept, never were in a dream like state. These wield great power, they can shape things not only in the ghost realm but within our own."
entries.zh:
这本书看起来不过是一些关于幽灵存在的荒诞理论的汇编，但有些段落的语气却截然不同。

“幽灵的领域中蕴藏着一种与生俱来的力量。它不同于物质世界，不受物质的束缚，也不遵循物理法则。幽灵可以凭空造出任何东西，无论是物体还是力量，只要一念便能使其存在，正如我们在梦中所做的那样。然而，这要求它们清楚地认识自身的处境，理解自己的领域及自身在其中的位置。大多数幽灵都在迷惘中游荡，任由扭曲的思想和感知摆布，但并非全部如此。有些已经醒来，或许它们从未沉睡，也从未陷入梦一般的状态。它们拥有强大的力量，不仅能够塑造幽灵领域中的事物，也能塑造我们世界中的事物。”

entries.en:
Life of Linus Fendrick by Anonymous.

A famous book with an even more famous story surrounding it, often told by mothers to their young children, a cautionary tale on the dark and sinister trappings of thaumaturgy. Fendrick was a gifted thaumaturge who lost his young wife and three children in some gruesome accident. He was thus driven to necromancy in the hope of resurrecting them, not the traditional crude raising of the dead, but with full sentience and cognizance. His practices and experiments were most vile in nature. Kidnappings, torture, murder, keeping his family's bodies in a state between life and death for some forty years; his crimes were plentiful and led to nothing save failure and despair.
entries.zh:
《莱纳斯·芬德里克传》，佚名著。

这本书很有名，书中的故事更是家喻户晓。母亲们常用它告诫年幼的孩子：异能之术潜藏着黑暗而险恶的诱惑。芬德里克是位天赋卓绝的异能术士，却在一场惨烈的意外中失去了年轻的妻子和三个孩子。为了让他们复活，他开始钻研死灵术。他追求的不是传统而粗陋的唤起死者，而是让他们带着完整的意识和认知归来。他的行径与实验极为邪恶：绑架、折磨、谋杀，让家人的尸身在生死之间维持了约四十年。他罪行累累，最终却只得到了失败与绝望。

entries.en:
The Forgotten Power by Anonymous

According to this book humans are powerful, immortal beings that have forgotten their true nature. That, by living your life by a certain moral code, performing certain rituals and eating a certain diet, you can achieve great power and ultimately unlock your dormant immortality.

《被遗忘的力量》，佚名著。

这本书声称，人类原本是强大而不朽的存在，只是忘记了自己的本性。只要遵循某种道德准则生活，举行特定的仪式，并采用特定的饮食，就能获得巨大的力量，最终唤醒沉睡的不朽之身。

entries.en:
Forgotten by Aime Koren.

A scholarly book about memory and cognizance. What we forget and why we forget it, how we choose to make a history for ourselves regardless of the facts, how we are defined by the wholly unreliable and subjective thing we call memory.
entries.zh:
《遗忘》，艾梅·科伦著。

一本研究记忆与认知的学术著作。书中探讨我们会忘记什么、为何会忘记，如何罔顾事实为自己编织过往，以及我们如何被记忆这种极不可靠、充满主观性的东西所定义。

entries.en:
This book explores various myths surrounding the Guardian but does so in what seems like a tendentious manner, casting him in a more positive light than he is commonly viewed in. You suspect it is tied to some cult dedicated to the worship of the Guardian.

The Guardian of the Underworld, known also as the Keeper of the Dead, is the most prominent figure in our mythology. As with most our myths it differs depending on whom you ask, the Guardian's role in particular is an ambivalent one. There is fear of what he represents and of his dark and dangerous realm but there is also a feeling of deference and a belief that he will watch over our loved ones once they pass away. We inter our dead to consign them to the Guardian's care and we believe that he will grant them a life beyond this one. Behind the intimidating titles and malicious curses the Guardian is also a giver of life. He is said to restore life to those that have fallen in his service, or that some become beholden to him owing to their resurrection. Perhaps the most notable myth is that in a time of dire need the Guardian will raise an army of those given into his care to defend us. What is it then that he guards? Does he simply watch over our dead and his dreadful realm or might it be that he is in fact our protector?
entries.zh:
这本书探讨了关于守护者的种种传说，但似乎刻意将他描绘得比世人通常认为的更加正面。你怀疑它与某个崇拜守护者的教派有关。

冥界守护者，也被称作亡者看守，是我们神话中最显赫的存在。和大多数传说一样，不同的人有不同的说法，而守护者的身份尤其矛盾。人们畏惧他所象征的事物，畏惧他那黑暗而危险的领域，却又心怀敬意，相信他会照看逝去的亲人。我们将死者埋入地下，把他们托付给守护者，相信他会赐予他们此生之后的另一段生命。在令人畏惧的名号和恶毒的诅咒背后，守护者也是生命的赐予者。据说他会使那些为他效力而死的人重获生命，也有人因复活之恩而臣服于他。最广为人知的传说或许是：危难之际，守护者会唤起那些托付于他的亡者，组成军队保卫我们。那么，他究竟守护着什么？他只是在看守我们的亡者和他那可怕的领域，还是说，他其实是我们的保护者？

entries.en: The Earth on which we walk is our mother, she provides for us all that we may need. Our ancestors, in their mad lust for power sought more, they began to dig deep into our Earth, in search of her lifeblood. And so by digging they uncovered the Underworld and its fearsome Guardian. He sent forth terrible demons to drive them out and hunt them down. Before all could be slain, our ancient kin sealed the entrances to the Underworld and swore never to return. Thus are we allowed to live upon this Earth, but ever under the watchful eye of the Guardian.
entries.zh: 我们脚下的大地是母亲，她赐予我们生活所需的一切。先祖却疯狂地渴望力量，不肯知足。他们向大地深处挖掘，寻找母亲的生命之血。于是，他们挖开了冥界，也惊动了可怖的守护者。他派出骇人的恶魔，驱逐并追猎他们。在所有人惨遭杀戮之前，古老的先民封住了冥界的入口，发誓永不返回。我们因而获准继续生活在大地上，却永远处于守护者的注视之下。

@WEAR00:瓶子是空的。

entries.en:
@WEAR75:A sphere with a strange pattern within. Its surface seems to shift when you press against it.

@WEAR00:A smooth black sphere.
entries.zh:
@WEAR75:一颗内部带有奇异纹路的球体。按压它时，表面似乎会流动。

@WEAR00:一颗光滑的黑色球体。

entries.en: This mace has large flanges that form a hollow space lined with strange decorative elements. [sc]
entries.zh: 这把钉头锤的大型凸缘围成了一个中空空间，内壁饰有奇异的装饰。[sc]
一枚带有装饰的小棋子

entries.en: A bottle with a protective wicker casing
entries.zh: 一只套有柳编护套的瓶子

entries.en: An ornate sceptre holding what seem to be very large gemstones. When you hold it you feel as though your mind can focus on more things at once. [sc]
entries.zh: 一柄华丽的权杖，上面镶着似乎极为硕大的宝石。握住它时，你觉得自己的心神仿佛能同时专注于更多事物。[sc]

entries.en: This intricately designed and articulated arm harness looks cumbersome, but undoubtedly effective. [sq]
entries.zh: 这套整臂甲设计精巧，关节结构复杂。看起来十分笨重，但防护无疑可靠。[sq]

entries.en: When you wear this strange helmet you feel a strong sense of quiet and isolation. [sc]
entries.zh: 戴上这顶奇异的头盔时，你会感到强烈的宁静，仿佛与世隔绝。[sc]

entries.en: A simple iron key attached to a collar.
entries.zh: 一把挂在项圈上的普通铁钥匙。

entries.en: An extremely large and heavy sword of unusual design. Its weight and grip make it impossible to use.
entries.zh: 一把设计独特、极其巨大沉重的剑。它的重量和握柄都让人无法使用。

entries.en: An enormous and heavy spear with a large bladed head.
entries.zh: 一柄庞大而沉重的长矛，带有宽大的刃状矛头。

entries.en: A heavy ornate armour made from a brass like metal. Various shield like elements appear to float and move with the armour without being attached to it. [sq]
entries.zh: 一套沉重华丽的护甲，由类似黄铜的金属制成。许多盾状部件并未与护甲连接，却仿佛悬浮在周围，随护甲一同移动。[sq]

entries.en: A large ornate spear set with gemstones. [sq]
entries.zh: 一柄镶嵌着宝石的大型华丽长矛。[sq]

entries.en: A prickling sensation washes over your body.
entries.zh: 一阵麻刺感掠过你的全身。

entries.en: A visored helm made from a metal similar to brass, but not as heavy as you expect. [sq]
entries.zh: 一顶带面甲的头盔，由类似黄铜的金属制成，却没有想象中那么重。[sq]

entries.en: As you touch the pendant a soothing sensation washes over you.
entries.zh: 触碰吊坠时，一阵舒缓的感觉传遍你的全身。

entries.en:
@WEAR50:The crystal is tightly clamped in the device, but can removed.

@WEAR00:The crystal seems to be fused to the device and cannot be removed.
entries.zh:
@WEAR50:水晶被牢牢夹在装置中，但可以取出。

@WEAR00:水晶似乎已与装置融为一体，无法取出。
